elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence: "Upon the expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, MSL will..." — it is not limited to termination for default, unlike the retained § 5.2 a) chapeau.

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: The insertion commits only to "a period of at least ninety (90) Days"; no six-month outer period is stated anywhere in the rendered language.

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
elements.evidence: No pricing basis appears in the inserted sentence or in retained § 5.2 a) ii); there is no reference to MSL's then-current rates.

elements.element: Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: "within thirty (30) Days after such expiration or termination MSL will export and deliver to IBM all IBM data in MSL's possession or control."

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: The export obligation specifies no format; the words "commonly used, machine-readable format" from the model language were not included.

elements.element: Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: No deletion or written-certification obligation follows the export sentence; retained § 5.2 a) iii) only addresses return of documentation and confidential media.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: "Upon the expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason" — covers both expiry and any termination, curing the default-only limit of the existing chapeau at p0121.

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: "provide the transition assistance described in Section 5.2 a) ii) for a period of at least ninety (90) Days"; the cross-referenced text (transfer of MSL responsibilities and Products to IBM or its designee) is a live, existing description, so the reference is not dangling. The "at IBM's request" condition is a Customer election, not a trigger tied to anticipated expiry only.

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: "within thirty (30) Days after such expiration or termination MSL will export and deliver to IBM all IBM data in MSL's possession or control" — a committed period replacing the redacted "[*] Days" gap in p0130.

reasons: Position-complete at the fallback: all three fallback elements are met in operative language (any expiry/termination trigger, ≥90 Days of assistance, 30-Day data export). The finding is correctly classified as a deviation because the existing § 5.2 a) ii) fixes no duration and § 5.2 a) iii) leaves the return period redacted as "[*] Days".

Preferred level is not reached: no six-month cap, no then-current-rates basis, no machine-readable format, and no post-return certified deletion. If the drafter wants the preferred package, these four items must be added expressly; the comment correctly declines to claim them.

Minimal: a single inserted sentence in the termination section, no deletion or paraphrase of retained language (including the Customer-favourable § 5.2 c) and § 5.2 a) iii)), and no extras such as survival tails, at-own-expense wording, or procedures beyond the selected checklist.

Preserves intent: retained § 5.2 a) iii) (return of IBM Product documentation and confidential media on the redacted timetable) operates cumulatively with the new data-export obligation and is not contradicted; the cross-reference to Section 5.2 a) ii) resolves to existing text.

Drafting caution (not a failure): "Days" is defined in § 1.3 as business days as followed by a particular Work Center, so "thirty (30) Days" runs longer and less determinately than 30 calendar days. Consider "thirty (30) calendar days" to match the playbook anchor exactly.

Optional improvement if reopened: add "in a commonly used, machine-readable format" to the export limb so the exported data is usable, and confirm "IBM data" is read to include all data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for IBM.
